Angela B: Heads-up — noticed a big drop in prefix cache hit-rate on canary after the tool-call serializer change. :eyes:
Kevin L: ugh, numbers? which canary and time window?
Angela B: canary c-3, 5m rolling. top-100 prefixes hit-rate went 87% -> 62% starting ~1987654200. p50 latency +9ms, p99 went 45ms -> 78ms.
Sylas M: grabbing profile now. initial look suggests cache key mismatches due to `tool` object ordering and a new `metadata` field we added in serialize().
Kevin L: that matches a few traces I saw — prefix key mismatch leading to more cold kernelfills and smaller batches.
Angela B: exact regression landed in deploy at 1987654100, code: `serializer:enable_metadata=true` flag.
deploy-bot: Deploy c-3:v42 to canary started by @maria at 1987654098.
Maria P: I can roll the flag back. before we do, can we confirm if pinning tokenizer version matters here?
Sylas M: good Q. I checked — tokenizer id stayed the same. This is purely key canonicalization: ordering + boolean field presence.
David R: so two levers: (1) make serializer stable/canonical (sort map keys, drop ephemeral metadata) (2) make cache key tolerant (normalize tool fields, hash-insensitive to order).
Kevin L: both are valid. (1) is safer long-term but needs careful compatibility handling for existing keys. (2) quick fix: add a compat-layer that normalizes before lookup.
Angela B: impact on batching: hitting fewer warm prefixes increases short-lived invocations, lowers batch sizes. we saw average batch size drop 3.2 -> 2.1 in the same window. kernel selection then falls back to low-latency kernels more often — net throughput down.
Sylas M: attaching quick diff I'm about to push for normalizing tool fields during key gen:
Sylas M: ```
- key = hash(prefix + json.dumps(tool))
+ tool_serial = canonical_serialize(tool, sort_keys=True, drop=['_trace_id','_temp_meta'])
+ key = stable_hash(prefix + tool_serial)
```
Kevin L: looks good. what about function-call args ordering? some customers pass dicts that are semantically unordered.
Maria P: canonical_serialize should recursively sort dictionaries and represent lists as-is. also add tokenizer_version into the key header so future tokenizer changes are pinned.
David R: we need to be careful with adding tokenizer_version — it will fragment the cache when we roll tokenizer updates. prefer to default to implicit pinning only when tokenizer actually changes model input lengths.
Angela B: for immediate mitigation I'm going to request rollback of `enable_metadata` on canary and schedule a hotfix that normalizes keys. canary rollback ok? @maria please do. :pray:
Maria P: rolling back flag now.
deploy-bot: Rollback c-3:v42 flag `serializer:enable_metadata` -> false requested by @Maria P at 1987654380.
Maria P: rollback applied, monitoring.
Sylas M: I'll prepare the hotfix branch with canonical_serialize + unit tests for round-trip idempotence and perf microbench. also adding an integration test that simulates 1k unique tool-orderings.
Kevin L: please add a metric for cache key entropy (e.g., unique keys per prefix / requests) so we can detect shifts automatically.
David R: agree. add an alert if top-500 prefix hit-rate drops >10% over 10m.
Angela B: follow-ups: 1) hotfix PR for normalization (Sylas), 2) add tokenizer pin discussion doc (David), 3) metrics/alert (Kevin), 4) retro when fixed (Angela).
Maria P: canary hit-rate trending back up already — 64% after rollback. will keep watching. :thumbsup:
Sylas M: pushing PR draft in ~20m, will include a script for synthetic warmup to rebuild cache keys post-deploy. snippet: 
Sylas M: ```bash
# rebuild cache for top prefixes after key change
python tools/warmup.py --prefix-list top_10k.txt --parallel 8 --verify-hitrate
```
Angela B: thanks. also let's add a short note to eng-runtime about being mindful when adding ephemeral fields to serializers. small change, big perf.
Kevin L: agreed. I'll take metrics/alert. ping me if we need rollback rehearsals.
David R: I'll draft the tokenizer pin pros/cons doc.
Maria P: closing loop once hotfix lands.
Angela B: great — thanks all. heading to standup to mention the rollback and hotfix.
